# `sim/fluids/FluidPhaseChange.js`

> **Source:** `engine/sim/fluids/FluidPhaseChange.js`

============================================================================= FLUID PHASE CHANGE - Freeze/Melt mechanics for fluid-rigid transitions ============================================================================= Implements phase transitions between fluid and solid states: - Freeze: Extract fluid region → spawn rigid body - Melt: Destroy rigid body → inject fluid mass/momentum

## Functions

### `createPhaseChangeBuffers(device, gridSize, maxParticles)`

Create phase change data structures

### `createSpellForce(position, direction, power, element)`

Spell force injection point

### `createSpellForceShader(workgroupSize = 256)`

Generate shader for applying spell forces to fluid

### `createFreezeShader(workgroupSize = 256)`

Generate shader for freeze effect (temperature-based phase transition)

### `createCrystallizationShader(workgroupSize = 256)`

Generate shader for particle-based crystallization chain reaction Physics-based with latent heat buffer, hysteresis, and asymmetric rates Key concepts from real physics: - Latent heat: Energy absorbed/released during phase change while temp stays constant - Hysteresis: Different thresholds for freezing vs melting (prevents flickering) - Supercooling: Fluid can stay liquid below freezing until nucleation occurs

### `createSolidCollisionShader(workgroupSize = 256)`

Generate shader for solid particle collision Frozen particles get rigid collision with world, entities, AND other particles Also handles temperature transfer on contact

### `createCrystalBondShader(workgroupSize = 256)`

Generate shader for crystal bond formation Finds nearby frozen particles and creates rigid bonds between them

### `createBondConstraintShader(workgroupSize = 256)`

Generate shader for bond constraint solving (Position-Based Dynamics) Maintains rigid crystal structure by keeping bonded particles at fixed distances

Create compute pipeline for solid particle collision

Create compute pipeline for bond constraint solving

## Constants

- `FluidPhase` — Phase states for fluid cells/particles
- `PARTICLE_PHASE_STRIDE` — Particle solidification attributes (per-particle) - temperature: Current temp (ambient ~20, freezing < 0) - magicSaturation: 0-1, how much "freeze magic" has accumulated - solidPhase: 0=fluid, 1=freezing, 2=frozen - seedStrength: If > 0, this particle spreads solidification
- `BOND_STRIDE` — Crystal bond attributes (per-bond) Stores connections between frozen particles forming crystal lattice - particleA: index of first particle - particleB: index of second particle - restDistance: original distance when bond formed (constraint target) - stiffness: bond strength (0-1, higher = more rigid)
- `MAX_BONDS_PER_PARTICLE`
- `DEFAULT_CRYSTAL_PARAMS` — Default crystallization parameters - tuned for fast freeze, slow melt
- `DEFAULT_SOLID_COLLISION_PARAMS` — Default solid collision parameters

## Notes & Examples

### Physics Engine Integration

The physics system provides rigid body dynamics, collision detection, and raycasting. Bodies have shapes (box, sphere, mesh), mass properties, and constraints. The GPU physics engine accelerates broad-phase collision detection and particle systems.

**Example: Creating physics bodies**
```js
import { PhysicsWorld } from 'engine/physics/PhysicsWorld.js';
import { RigidBody } from 'engine/physics/RigidBody.js';
import { BoxShape, SphereShape } from 'engine/physics/Shapes.js';

const world = new PhysicsWorld({ gravity: [0, -9.8, 0] });

// Static ground
const ground = new RigidBody({
  type: 'static',
  shape: new BoxShape(10, 1, 10),
  position: [0, -0.5, 0]
});
world.addBody(ground);

// Dynamic box
const box = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  mass: 1,
  shape: new BoxShape(1, 1, 1),
  position: [0, 5, 0],
  restitution: 0.5  // Bounciness
});
world.addBody(box);
```

**Advanced: Collision detection and raycasting**
```js
// Raycast to find what the player is looking at
const hit = world.raycast(camera.position, camera.forward, 100);
if (hit) {
  console.log('Hit entity:', hit.body.entityId);
  console.log('Hit point:', hit.point);
  console.log('Hit normal:', hit.normal);
  
  // Apply impulse at hit point
  hit.body.applyImpulse([0, 10, 0], hit.point);
}

// Shapecast (swept sphere) for character movement
const sweep = world.shapecast(
  player.position,           // Start
  desiredPosition,           // End
  new SphereShape(0.5),    // Player capsule radius
  { ignore: player.body }  // Don't collide with self
);
if (sweep.hit) {
  // Slide along wall
  player.position = sweep.position;
}
```

**Advanced: Constraints and joints**
```js
import { HingeConstraint, FixedConstraint } from 'engine/physics/Constraints.js';

// Door hinge
const doorHinge = new HingeConstraint({
  bodyA: doorFrame,
  bodyB: door,
  pivot: [0, 1, 0],      // Hinge location
  axis: [0, 1, 0],       // Hinge axis (Y up)
  limits: [-90, 90]      // Open angle range in degrees
});
world.addConstraint(doorHinge);

// Ragdoll joint (ball-and-socket)
const shoulder = new FixedConstraint({
  bodyA: torso,
  bodyB: arm,
  pivotA: [0.5, 1.5, 0],  // Shoulder position on torso
  pivotB: [0, 0, 0]       // Shoulder position on arm
});
world.addConstraint(shoulder);
```

**Advanced: Continuous collision detection (CCD)**
```js
// Fast-moving objects need CCD to not tunnel through walls
const projectile = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  shape: new SphereShape(0.1),
  mass: 0.1,
  ccd: { enabled: true, sweptSphereRadius: 0.1 },
  linearDamping: 0  // No air resistance for bullets
});
projectile.velocity = [0, 0, 100];  // Very fast
world.addBody(projectile);
```

**Gotchas:**
- **Units**: Physics uses meters, kilograms, seconds. A 1-unit cube is 1 meter.
- **Time step**: Fixed time step (1/60) gives stable simulation; variable dt causes explosions.
- **Collision layers**: Use collision masks to filter what collides (player vs enemy, bullet vs world).
- **Sleeping**: At-rest bodies sleep to save CPU — wake them before applying forces.
